stem: Two towns each have 10,000 residents and complete outcome follow-up for the same outbreak period. Town A has 100 cases and 10 disease-related deaths. Town B has 500 cases and 10 disease-related deaths. Which of the following comparisons is supported by these counts?

options.label: A
options.text: A has higher case fatality and higher disease-specific mortality
options.explanation: Case fatality is higher in A because ten deaths occur among fewer cases. Population mortality is equal, however, because both towns have ten disease deaths among 10,000 residents.
options.misconception: Infers greater population mortality from greater fatality among cases.

options.label: B
options.text: A has lower case fatality and equal disease-specific mortality
options.explanation: The mortality comparison is correct, but case fatality is 10/100 in A and 10/500 in B. A therefore has the higher fatality proportion among affected people.
options.misconception: Reverses the fatality comparison despite fewer cases per death in A.

options.label: C
options.text: A has equal case fatality and lower disease-specific mortality
options.explanation: Equal death counts do not imply equal case fatality when case counts differ. Both population size and disease deaths are equal, so the disease-specific mortality comparison is also incorrect.
options.misconception: Ignores unequal case denominators and misreads equal population mortality.

options.label: D
options.text: A has equal case fatality and higher disease-specific mortality
options.explanation: Case fatality differs because the towns have different numbers of cases. Disease-specific mortality is equal because the disease death counts and population denominators are the same.
options.misconception: Treats equal death counts as equal case fatality but unequal mortality.

options.label: E
options.text: A has higher case fatality and equal disease-specific mortality
options.explanation: Case fatality is 10% in A and 2% in B, so it is higher in A. Disease-specific mortality is 10/10,000 in each town over the same interval.
options.misconception: No misconception: case fatality differs while population mortality is equal.

context:
Learning objective: Use case and population denominators separately when comparing fatality and mortality across outbreaks.

Case fatality is 10% in A and 2% in B, so it is higher in A. Disease-specific mortality is 10/10,000 in each town over the same interval.
